scenarios.theme: Can a five-second shaping queue serve a 300 ms interactive request?
scenarios.assumptions: The system delays excess work for seconds and calls it throttling. Callers time out and retry before execution starts. What policy fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Rate Limiting & Throttling to queue vs deadline.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Can a five-second shaping queue serve a 300 ms interactive request?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Bound waiting by the remaining interactive deadline and queue resource budget, then refuse excess work early with a truthful response

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A queue can smooth short bursts when useful completion remains possible, but long waiting can create duplicate attempts and wasted work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Merely returning a longer client timeout changes the contract and may worsen resource retention.

scenarios.theme: Three layers each allow four attempts during overload. What is the trap?
scenarios.assumptions: A caller, gateway and service each retry a failed downstream operation independently. One request can cause a multiplicative attempt tree. What will you change?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Rate Limiting & Throttling to retry multiplication.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Three layers each allow four attempts during overload. What is the trap?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Choose an intentional retry owner, bound attempts and total retry demand, propagate remaining deadlines and use jitter

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Four attempts at three layers can produce up to 64 deepest-layer attempts in a simplified worst case

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Removing every retry may reduce resilience to a transient fault; retain only justified bounded recovery.

scenarios.theme: Each of twenty replicas enforces a local 100/s limit. Is the global API capped at 100/s?
scenarios.assumptions: The policy is intended as an aggregate protection boundary, but requests spread across replicas and scaling changes the total. What will you decide?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Rate Limiting & Throttling to global budget.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Each of twenty replicas enforces a local 100/s limit. Is the global API capped at 100/s?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: State whether the budget is per-instance or shared, and implement/document an aggregate mechanism or deliberate allocation/approximation across replicas

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: A coordinated limiter adds latency/availability and state consistency trade-offs; local coarse protection remains useful even with a global policy

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Do not advertise an exact global bound from independent local counters or assume a managed gateway makes every quota exact.
